kind: Repeated event and native-stage timing of the current deployed Riemann GUI
methodology: Two sequential fresh-browser captures at normal motion without throttling; the same 175187-file project and 15-declaration compiled graph. Profiling finished before validation workloads began.

Dispatch is synchronous browser event processing. Input-to-two-rAF includes browser scheduling; it is not physical presentation or field INP. Nested intervals overlap; sampled CPU share is not wall-time share. Small within-run p95 samples are diagnostic, not field percentiles.

Fit View is measured separately. Eight initial/repeated selections are followed by eight switches alternating two distinct declarations. Each click uses a real pointer hit and must reveal its exact original source line. Three frames settle each click. This is not an all-declaration or rapid-click workload.

Browser automation selectors and hit tests contribute CPU samples; do not assign all query/anonymous work to the application. Exact graph camera transforms and per-selection target identities are retained.

Native spans retain the original monotonic IDs and exact worker sampling manifests. The bounded ring evicted 0 / 214 records during the two captures; new native-stage summaries exclude IDs already present at each capture start.

All seven actual served JavaScript bundles were compared byte-for-byte with the hidden-source-map build. The executable matched its immutable deployment digest. No server restart or model request was performed.

initial_preparation.scope: Single initial fill of the current compiler/search cache with installed Lean and existing project/OS dependencies, not cold installation. The exploratory browser script later failed because its source-line assertion used the demo reader selector instead of the native editor selector. That selector was corrected, and none of this incomplete attempt's gesture timings or unfinished sampling recording is counted as a successful capture.

manifest.limits: Current-user native host and inherited workers only; no kernel stacks. Thread CPU spans exclude worker CPU. File preparation reuses project/OS caches, not a cold installation. Sampling changes timing; browser profiles have their own overhead.
